name: lasso
desc: Library for Liberty Alliance and SAML protocols
why: A door into SAML and Liberty Alliance federated login, the XML trust machinery behind many single sign-on setups, though it is a library more than a toy.

brief.what_it_is: Lasso is a free C library that implements the Liberty Alliance standards for federated identity and single sign-on. It is built on libxml2, XMLSec and OpenSSL. It takes SAML and Liberty protocol messages in and produces or verifies them, so applications can handle identity provider and service provider roles. The homepage says it is 'just a library': applications must use it to implement the profiles themselves. Language bindings are generated with SWIG.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes Lasso as a 'Free Liberty Alliance Implementation' that 'defines processes for federated identities, single sign-on and related protocols.' It began with the Liberty Alliance ID-FF 1.2 protocols and later added ID-WSF and SAML 2.0 support.
brief.how_it_works: Lasso is a C library with XML and cryptographic code underneath (libxml2, XMLSec, OpenSSL). Applications call it to build and process protocol messages for each supported profile. SWIG generates high-level bindings for Python, Perl, Java and PHP, with preliminary .NET assemblies. The homepage's support matrix lists which IdP and SP profiles are marked OK, including Single Sign-On (Artifact, Browser POST, LECP), Single Logout over HTTP-Redirect, HTTP-GET and SOAP, Federation Termination Notification, Name Identifier Registration, Identity Provider Introduction, Attribute Query and Authorization Decision Query.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install commands. Dependencies named are libxml2, XMLSec and OpenSSL. Bindings are offered for Python, Perl, Java and PHP, with preliminary .NET. The homepage says the project is developed primarily on GNU/Linux and also works on many UNIX systems including macOS and Microsoft Windows. The Download page was linked from the homepage, but I did not follow it, so build and install steps are unverified.
brief.standout: Lasso is a rare open implementation of the Liberty Alliance federation stack, and it is still maintained with 2025 releases. Its support matrix is explicit about which profiles work on each side, which helps when judging fit for an existing SAML deployment.
brief.status: Maintained, judging by the homepage. Latest release is 2.9.0, dated 2025-08-12, with a changelog covering libxml2 2.12 and XMLSec 1.3.0 compatibility and Python 3.14 test fixes. The previous release, 2.8.2, is dated 2023-03-14. The footer still reads 'Copyright 2004-2010', which looks stale but does not affect the release news. I did not check the repository or commit history.
brief.caveats: This is a library, not a standalone SSO server or command-line tool, so an application has to be built on top of it. Its homepage describes it as implementing Liberty Alliance standards, and the support matrix covers the profiles listed above, not every part of the specs. Licensing is GPL with an OpenSSL exception, and a commercial license is available for proprietary use. The homepage says the project is primarily developed on GNU/Linux. The Homebrew entry has no executables and no caveats.
quotes: Lasso is a free software C library aiming to implement the Liberty Alliance standards; it defines processes for federated identities, single sign-on and related protocols.
Lasso is just a library, it is up to the applications to use it to implement profiles defined by the Liberty Alliance.
We strongly recommend the use of the GNU General Public License each time it is possible. But for proprietary projects, that wouldn't want to use it, we designed a commercial license.
fetch_log: https://lasso.entrouvert.org/ : fetched OK. Contains news, a description, and a support matrix. It has no install commands and no explicit documentation or download URLs, so I did not follow further links and did not guess any.
